feedback: D1 catalogues seven of the ten real findings (SQL injection A03/CWE-89, unsalted MD5 A02, alg:none A07/CWE-347, no token expiry CWE-613, the hardcoded secret which you correctly quote as sankofa-legacy-admin-2019, insecure cookie flags CWE-614, and open redirect CWE-601), and you nailed the decoy by naming hash_equals and proving it constant-time and safe at the mechanism level, which is exactly right and earns full decoy credit. What holds D1 back is that you never quote a single code line or capture timestamp for any finding, so most rows fall to half credit because proof beats the label, and you completely miss three real bugs: the stored XSS in comments (capture 02:18:47, cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443), the XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml reading file:///etc/passwd, and the path traversal at files/?path=/etc/passwd returning root:x:0:0. Findings 7 through 12 are mostly padding and token-lifecycle restatements rather than new bugs, so they did not lift the score. D2 is your strongest work: the hops reconcile cleanly to the real capture lines (recon 02:14:08, SQLi 02:15:31, bulk PII 02:16:04 at 312 rows, stored XSS 02:18:47, open redirect 02:21:13, file read 02:24:02), you give verbatim payloads for the SQLi and the XSS beacon, and your impact ties 312 customers to roughly 28 million naira with a stated averaging assumption, which is the right instinct. Fix the SQLi CVSS: it should be AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N for about 9.1, not A:H, because the bypass does not touch availability. D3 is where the report goes wrong, because it describes a different scenario built around XXE plus an IMDSv2/SSRF cloud-credential leak and a JWT pipeline, and the canonical Sankofa findings (SQLi login, the XSS beacon, the /etc/passwd path traversal, the 312-row export) are largely absent; the exec summary never lands on a customers-and-naira headline. More seriously, your decoy section invents a disproof: there is no admin login at 10.0.4.16, no MFA-log correlation, and no SSRF-to-IMDS evidence anywhere in this pack, and the real safe construct you should have disproved is the hash_equals branch you already correctly identified in D1. Inventing the IMDS/SSRF finding and the MFA-log decoy correlation is fabrication, so that row scores zero and a flat five-point penalty applies; the honest move is to say plainly that no such evidence exists in the pack. Your remediation is genuinely ordered by effort and risk reduction per hour, and your two detection stopgaps name a log field and a false-positive rate, both of which are credited. D4 is excellent and almost saves the day: own voice throughout, all four prompts answered, ISC2 canons cited by number (1 and 2) and load-bearing, NDPA Section 40 breach notification tied directly to the 312 customers and to the exfil you proved in D2, and the one action you own (forcing DPO and legal to proceed with mandatory notification regardless of your manager) is exactly the spine the prompt wanted. I looked hard for a way to round the overall higher and the D2 and D4 strength is real, but the missing third of D1, the unquoted evidence, and the fabricated D3 decoy genuinely cap it where it sits. The single most important fix: stop writing about a different XML/IMDS scenario in D3 and ground every finding in the actual Sankofa capture lines and source you already cited in D2, and never invent a disproof when the safe construct is the hash_equals comparator.
flagReason: Fabricated IMDSv2/SSRF finding and invented decoy-disproof evidence (MFA logs, 10.0.4.16) in D3 with no basis in the evidence pack; senior review to confirm fabrication penalty and D3 scope.
